name: Kerr parametric oscillator, 1.5 stored photons
question: Does a few-photon Kerr parametric oscillator, swept through threshold with a bias, choose its state by the linear stage or by the balance of its two shallow wells?
assumptions: Frame rotating at half the pump frequency; hbar = 1; rates in units of the single-photon loss kappa.
The Kerr coefficient equals the loss, so the stored states hold about 1.5 photons at the end of the ramp.
The bias is the one for which the Gaussian-stage law would predict 0.90 at a sweep rate of 0.01; here the rate is 0.1.
A control of the linear-stage law: the exact probability is expected at the selection of the biased steady state.

provenance.reference: few-photon Kerr parametric oscillators of Z. Wang et al., Phys. Rev. X 9, 021049 (2019) and N. E. Frattini et al., Phys. Rev. X 14, 031040 (2024)
